## Introduction and overview {#intro}

  ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Module                  Machine Learning — SynapseS 2026-2027 sheet: "Programme d'approfondissement — Bases de l'Apprentissage Automatique" (occurrence: "Foundations of Machine Learning")
  Code                    MDC_51006_EP
  Team and workload       Course coordinators: Erwan Le Pennec & Jesse Read (École Polytechnique, CMAP) · 36 h in person (2026-2027 catalog, max enrollment 144) · 4.5 ECTS · language of instruction: English · the methodological foundation of the program: supervised and unsupervised learning, from least squares to boosting, together with the accompanying generalization theory.
  Status in the program   [Mandatory]{.badge .mandatory} M1 · S1 / period 1 (fall semester, from 17/09/26 to 18/12/26)
  ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Audience**: engineer who already fitted a sklearn model / MNIST-like MLP and wants to understand *why* it generalizes (or not) — without opening on VC dimension. **Empirical first**: visible overfitting on a train/test split, ridge that "calibrates" coefficients, a forest that works when linear fails.

Mandatory module: methodological foundation — learning from data, and under what conditions it works. Supervised (least squares → boosting), unsupervised, generalization theory. This is what separates understanding models from calling a library. Downstream LLGA (DL, NLP, Graph ML, RL) reuses this vocabulary.

### What you will be able to do

-   Frame a learning problem: risk, empirical risk, hypotheses, bias-variance trade-off.
-   Implement and tune linear regression, ridge/Lasso regularization, logistic regression and SVMs, justifying every choice.
-   Use kernels to move to the nonlinear setting and understand what a "reproducing kernel Hilbert space" brings in practice.
-   Choose between trees, random forests and boosting (gradient boosting) according to the nature of the data and the interpretability constraint.
-   Conduct a complete unsupervised analysis: k-means, Gaussian mixture and EM, PCA and dimensionality reduction.
-   State and exploit generalization bounds to argue for a model's performance on new data.
-   Build a rigorous evaluation pipeline: splits, cross-validation, adapted metrics, scaling up.
-   Read an academic or industrial ML paper and identify the underlying statistical framework.

### Official objectives and syllabus (2026-2027 catalog)

**Official objectives** (paraphrased from the description published on SynapseS): machine learning is the discipline that designs algorithms allowing computers to learn from data, automatically extract complex patterns from them and derive intelligent decisions from them. The course focuses on the *methodology underlying supervised and unsupervised learning*, with a particular emphasis on the *mathematical formulation of the algorithms* and on how they can be *implemented and used in practice*; to this end it presents the necessary tools from optimization theory. Proofs are not done in lecture: some are done in labs, others deferred to a document; every session ends with a numerical lab in Python. **Official assessment: a final exam.** The detailed session-by-session program is not published on the sheet ("not communicated"); the following table maps the elements of the official description to our chapters.

  Element of the official description                      Section of the course covering it
  -------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Methodology of **supervised** learning                   ch. 1 (statistical framework), ch. 2 (regression, regularization), ch. 3 (logistic, SVM), ch. 5 (trees, forests, boosting)
  Methodology of **unsupervised** learning                 ch. 6 (k-means, EM, PCA)
  **Mathematical formulation** of the algorithms           the guiding thread of all chapters, ch. 1 to 7
  Implementation and use **in practice**                   Python labs of the chapters, ch. 9 (evaluation, big data, pipelines)
  **Optimization theory** tools for ML                     ch. 0 (review: gradient, convexity), ch. 2 and 3 (regularized optimization, margins)
